Short title extent and commencement

ACT LVIII OF 1952
ACT LVIII OF 1952
PREVENTION
OF SMUGGLING ACT, 1952
1. Short title, extent and commencement.‑This Act may be
called the Prevention of Smuggling Act, 1952.
(2) It extends to all the
Provinces, the Capital of the Federation, the State of Bahawalpur and the
Baluch States Union.
(3) It shall come into force in
such areas and on such dates as the Central Government may, by notification,
direct.

Definitions

ACT LVIII OF 1952
ACT LVIII OF 1952
PREVENTION
OF SMUGGLING ACT, 1952
2. Definitions.‑In this Act, unless there is anything repugnant
in the subject or context,‑
(i) "notification"
means a notification published in the Official Gazette, and
"notified" shall be construed accordingly ;
(ii) "notified
commodity" means any commodity which the Central Government may, from time
to time, declare, by notification, to be a commo dity to which the provisions
of this Act shall apply ;
(iii) "possession"
with its grammatical variations and cognate expressions, shall include
possession through another person ;
(iv) "prescribed"
means prescribed by rules made under this Act.

Restriction on possession and movement of notified commodities

ACT LVIII OF 1952
ACT LVIII OF 1952
PREVENTION
OF SMUGGLING ACT, 1952
3. Restriction on possession and movement of notified commodities.--- As
from the date notified for this purpose, no person shall‑--
(a) have in his possession or
under his control any quantity of any notified commodity in any area to which
this Act applies, or
(b) move, carry, take or send
by any means whatsoever, any notified commodity to any place out of any area to
which this Act applies, unless such person complies with such conditions as may
be prescribed.

Penalties

ACT LVIII OF 1952
ACT LVIII OF 1952
PREVENTION
OF SMUGGLING ACT, 1952
4. Penalties.‑(1) Whoever contravenes any provision of section 3
shall, notwithstanding anything to the contrary contained in any other law for
the time being in force, be punishable‑--
(i) if the offence is tried
summarily, with imprisonment which may extend to one year and with fine ; and
(ii) if the offence is not
tried summarily, with imprisonment which may extend to five years and with
fine.
(2) A Court convicting any
person under this section may impose on him the sentence of whipping in lieu of
or in addition to any other punishment.
(3) A Court convicting any
person under this section shall order the forfeiture to the Government of any
notified commodity in respect of which the contravention has occurred, together
with any animal, vehicle, vessel or con tained seized therewith :‑--
Provided that no order of
confiscation of any animal, vehicle, vessel or container shall be made unless
it is proved that the owner of such animal, vehicle, vessel or container knew
or had reason to believe that his animal, vehicle, vessel or container was
being used for purposes of the contravention.

Attempt and abetment

ACT LVIII OF 1952
ACT LVIII OF 1952
PREVENTION
OF SMUGGLING ACT, 1952
5. Attempt and abetment.---‑Any
person who attempts to contravene any provision of section 3 or abets such
contravention, shall be deemed to have contravened such provision.

Power to try offences summarily

ACT LVIII OF 1952
ACT LVIII OF 1952
PREVENTION
OF SMUGGLING ACT, 1952
6. Power to try offences summarily.---‑Any
Magistrate for the time being empowered to try in a summary way the offences
specified in subsection (1) of section 260 of the Code of Criminal Procedure,
1898, may, on application in this behalf being made by the prosecution, try an
offence under this Act in accordance with the provisions of subsection (1) of
section 262 and sections 263 to 265 of that Code.

Special powers of Magistrates

ACT LVIII OF 1952
ACT LVIII OF 1952
PREVENTION
OF SMUGGLING ACT, 1952
7. Special powers of Magistrates.----‑Notwithstanding
anything con tained in the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, it shall be lawful
for any Magistrate of the First Class specially empowered by the Provincial
Government in this behalf to pass a sentence of imprisonment for a term
exceeding two years and of fine exceeding one thousand rupees on any person
convicted of contravening any provision of section 3.

Arrest and detention etc

ACT LVIII OF 1952
ACT LVIII OF 1952
PREVENTION
OF SMUGGLING ACT, 1952
8. Arrest and detention, etc.‑(1) The Central Government may authorise
any officer or person to arrest, detain or take into custody, any person who
contravenes or is suspected to have contravened or is likely to contravence,
the provisions of section 3, and to seize any notified com modity, in respect
of which such contravention has occurred or is suspected to have occurred or is
likely to occur, together with any animal, vehicle, vessel or container used or
likely to be used for such contravention.
(2) Any officer or person
authorised under subsection (1) may, for the purpose of arresting, detaining or
taking into custody, or preventing the escape of, any person who has committed
or is suspected to have com mitted or is likely to commit such contravention or
for the purpose of seizing or preventing the removal of any notified commodity
in respect of which such contravention has occurred or is suspected to have
occurred or is likely to occur, use or cause to be used such force, to the
extent of causing death as may be necessary.
(3) Any person in possession or
control of such notified commodity or animal, vehicle, vessel or container
shall proceed with the same to such place or places as the officer or person
making the seizure may require.

Public servant

ACT LVIII OF 1952
ACT LVIII OF 1952
PREVENTION
OF SMUGGLING ACT, 1952
9. Public servant.‑Every officer or person duly exercising
any power under the provisions of this Act shall be deemed to be a public
servant within the meaning of section 21 of
the Pakistan Penal Code, 1860.

Indemnity

ACT LVIII OF 1952
ACT LVIII OF 1952
PREVENTION
OF SMUGGLING ACT, 1952
10. Indemnity.---‑(1) No suit, prosecution or other legal
Proceedings shall lie against any person for anything which is in good faith
done or intended to be done. in pursuance of this Act.
(2) No suit or other legal proceedings shall lie against the
Government for any damage caused or likely to be caused by anything which is in
good faith done or intended to be done in pursuance of this Act. ,

Power to make rules

ACT LVIII OF 1952
ACT LVIII OF 1952
PREVENTION
OF SMUGGLING ACT, 1952
11. Power to make rules.‑The Central Government
may make rules for carrying out the purposes of this Act. .

Exemption

ACT LVIII OF 1952
ACT LVIII OF 1952
PREVENTION
OF SMUGGLING ACT, 1952
12. Exemption.‑‑The Central Government may, by
notification, ex empt any person or class of persons from all or any of the
provisions of this Act subject to such conditions, if any, as may be specified in
such notification.

Delegation of powers

ACT LVIII OF 1952
ACT LVIII OF 1952
PREVENTION
OF SMUGGLING ACT, 1952
13. Delegation of powers.‑The Central Government may, by notifi cation,
direct that all or any of the powers or duties which under: tire provisions of
this Act or rules made thereunder. are conferred .or imposed upon the Central
Government, shall be exercised or, ,'discharged by . any officer or authority
subordinate 'to it or by they .Provincial. Government ; and the Provincial
Government may, by a like notification, direct that all or any of the powers or
duties, as aforesaid, to be exercised or dis charged by it, shall be exercised
and discharged by any officer or authority subordinate to it.

Continuance of existing orders

ACT LVIII OF 1952
ACT LVIII OF 1952
PREVENTION
OF SMUGGLING ACT, 1952
14. Continuance of existing orders.‑All orders made under the
Pre vention of Smuggling Ordinance, 1952,
and in force immediately before the commencement of this Act, shall, so far
as they are not inconsistent with the provisions of. this Act, continue in
force and shall be deemed to have been made under this Act.

Repeal of ordinance VII of 1952

ACT LVIII OF 1952
ACT LVIII OF 1952
PREVENTION
OF SMUGGLING ACT, 1952
15. Repeal of Ordinance VII of
1952.‑The prevention of Smuggling Ordinance, 1955, is hereby repealed.
